```{r}
#| label: setup

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(toolero)
```

## Input Resolution

```{r}
#| label: input-resolution

# resolve_input_path() works out where the data lives, which depends on
# where this code is running. Three environments, three answers:
#
#   interactive : you are running chunks in RStudio -- the local copy of
#                 the data, for development convenience
#   quarto      : the document is being rendered -- the path comes from
#                 the params block in the YAML header above
#   rscript     : the document is running on a remote cluster -- the path
#                 arrives as the first command line argument
#
# Only the branch matching the current context is evaluated, so the
# params reference below is safe under Rscript, where params does not
# exist at all.

input_file <- resolve_input_path(
  interactive = "data-raw/sample.csv",
  quarto      = params$input_file,
  rscript     = commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)[1]
)

# The three arguments are spelled out here because seeing them is the
# point of this template. In your own document you can leave them off:
# the rscript branch defaults to the first command line argument, and the
# other two fall back to params$input_file, which makes the YAML header
# the single place the path is written.
#
#   input_file <- resolve_input_path()
```

## Load Data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

# read_clean_csv() reads the file and standardizes column names
# using janitor::clean_names() -- spaces and special characters
# are replaced with underscores and names are lowercased.

penguins <- read_clean_csv(input_file)

glimpse(penguins)
```

## Analysis

```{r}
#| label: summary

# A simple grouped summary across species.
# Replace this block with your own analysis.

p_stats <- penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    n            = n(),
    mean_mass    = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_flipper = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

p_stats
```

```{r}
#| label: plot

# Relationship between flipper length and body mass by species.
# Replace this block with your own plot.
#
# Data: a subset of the Palmer Archipelago penguin data, from an earlier
# version of the palmerpenguins package. Since R 4.5.0 the same data is
# in base R as datasets::penguins, with four columns renamed there:
# bill_len, bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass. See ?create_qmd for the
# full citation.
# https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0090081

p_plot <- penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title    = "Flipper Length vs Body Mass",
    subtitle = "By species -- Palmer Penguins dataset",
    x        = "Flipper length (mm)",
    y        = "Body mass (g)",
    color    = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_plot
```

## Save Results

```{r}
#| label: save-results

# Write outputs to an output/ folder in the working directory.
# When this script runs locally, results appear alongside your project.
# When it runs on a cluster via submitr, the executable script (.sh)
# packages this folder into a tarball for transfer.

output_dir <- "output"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write_clean_csv(
  p_stats,
  file.path(output_dir, "results.csv"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "plot.png"),
  plot     = p_plot
)
```
